title: 2021 The First Year
about: A reflection on my first full year as an Assistant Director and the beginning of a new chapter at State Arts-In.
description: After years of experiencing State Arts-In as a participant, becoming an Assistant Director changed how I saw the program. The halls and people were familiar, but the badge around my neck represented a completely different responsibility. Instead of simply being part of the experience, I was now helping create it for everyone else. The days were long, the nights were short, and responsibilities seemed to multiply constantly. Along the way came morning shows, masks, late nights, new ideas, unexpected problems, and friendships strengthened through the work. None of those moments alone defined the year, but together they marked the beginning of a new road and helped shape the person I would become. I originally wanted the music to carry a construction-inspired background, reflecting both the work of the year and the idea of building something new. Finding construction sounds that could be cleanly cued into the music wasn't practical, so the final track doesn't carry that element, even though the idea of construction remains at the heart of the story.
lyrics: I walked through doors I'd known for years,
The same old halls, familiar faces,
Yet nothing felt quite the same.
A different badge hung from my neck,
I wasn't there to simply join...
I was there to help each day.
Behind every moment on the stage
I finally stood on the other side
The first step down a brand new road.
To carry part of the load.
The mornings always came too soon,
The evenings stayed far too late.
Somewhere between the work and laughter,
Between the plans and every task,
The hardest weeks can leave behind
Sometimes they're built on shared laughter...
When every challenge taught me more.
Not because it all was easy,
Some help you grow in return.
Late nights that turned into early mornings.
A problem that sparked an idea.
Looking back, none of it seemed important by itself.
Not all at once, not overnight,
The work would end, the fair move on,
Still, part of who I am today
